reader.requirement: At --std 85 the computer-name of the Segmentation-module OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph must be a system-name: a COBOL word of at most 30 characters drawn from A-Z, 0-9 and hyphen (not first or last), not a reserved word of this edition, and (the types being disjoint) not one of the implementation's implementor-names; any such word, including one a later edition reserves, is accepted with MEMORY SIZE and SEGMENT-LIMIT.

edition-consulted.switches: a word reserved only in a later edition (TYPEDEF) is a free computer-name at 85; at 2023 it is reserved and refused
Year < 2002 only: a computer-name that is one of the implementation's implementor-names (device, feature, switch, code-name) is refused, COBOL7624 (the 1985 disjointness of system-name types)
ConstructRegistry ComputerNameOptional2002: clauses without a computer-name refused below 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a later-reserved word is a legal computer-name, an implementor-name is refused as one, and the clauses require a computer-name; 2002+ relaxes the last two and reserves more words
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover legal names, the clause sequence and later-reserved words as computer-names; reserved, underscore, over-long, trailing-hyphen and implementor-name refusals were probed here

probes.expected: WISE-OWL-PC1 with MEMORY SIZE 8 MODULES and SEGMENT-LIMIT IS 10 accepted
TYPEDEF is no 1985 reserved word, so a valid system-name at 85
refused: a reserved word (DATA) must not appear as a system-name

reader.notes: System-name formation is implementor-defined beyond the character set; this implementation accepts every well-formed non-reserved COBOL word that is not one of its implementor-names. The reserved-word refusal surfaces as a generic parse error, not a computer-name diagnostic; the refusal is correct.

refuter.evidence: Class c: words reserved in 1985, several no longer reserved in later editions (ENTER, RERUN, TEXT, QUEUE), as the computer-name: each refused at 85 (COBOL1970, exit 65), so the 1985 reserved list is applied to system-names, as §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3 requires. oc_lower.cob: a lowercase computer-name 'wise-pc-9' with MEMORY SIZE 100 WORDS and SEGMENT-LIMIT IS 49 was accepted and RAN (lowercase is equivalent). oc_lead.cob '-PC': COBOL2773, leading hyphen refused. oc_digits.cob '3090': refused (COBOL0900/COBOL1970). That refusal is implementor latitude ('Rules for the formation of a system-name are defined by the implementor'), and an all-digit string lexes as a numeric literal, not a COBOL word. cite.py: OK  §1985:XVI.2.2.3 SR1  (║2.2.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR1; OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2  (4.2.2.1.2 System-Names)  the text is in the clause; OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3  (4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words)  the text is in the clause.
